sections.h2: Where is Ballard County and how did it start?
sections.html:
Ballard County fills the far western tip of Kentucky where the Ohio River meets the Mississippi, in the Jackson Purchase. The county's own site calls it the ninety-third county formed, established February 15, 1842, from parts of Hickman and McCracken, and says it covers 254 square miles. Wikipedia's Census-based total is 274 square miles, of which 27 are water.

The first seat was Blandville. A courthouse fire on February 17, 1880 burned most early records, and Wickliffe took over as seat in 1882. Anyone tracing an old parcel should ask the County Clerk what survives for the years before 1880.

sections.h2: Which towns and neighborhoods share the same tax offices?
sections.html:
Barlow, Kevil, La Center and Wickliffe are the four cities, and La Center is the largest. Bandana and Lovelaceville are census-designated places. The entire population counted as rural in 2020, and one school system, Ballard County Schools, serves all of it. Axe Lake Swamp State Nature Preserve, 458 acres in the Barlow Bottoms, is part of a 3,000-acre wetland complex.

Water marks three sides of the county. Across the Ohio River sit Pulaski and Alexander counties in Illinois, and across the Mississippi sits Mississippi County, Missouri. McCracken County, home to the Paducah area, borders Ballard on the east and Carlisle County on the south, and the county belongs to the Paducah, Kentucky and Illinois metropolitan area.

Every one of these places pays through the same three courthouse-area offices:

  • Sheriff, 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe: bills and payments, (270) 335-3561 or (270) 335-5153.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: assessments and exemptions, (270) 335-3400.
  • County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: appeals and, later, unpaid bills, (270) 335-5168.

sections.h2: Is Ballard County growing or shrinking?
sections.html:
It is shrinking slowly. The population peaked at 14,378 in 1880, fell 41.6 percent to 8,390 by 1890, stayed between 7,900 and 8,800 from 1950 through 2010. The 2020 count was 7,728, a 6.3 percent drop, and the 2025 estimate is 7,594. The 2020 census found 3,228 households, 29.3 percent of them one person living alone and 14.8 percent a person 65 or older living alone.

A seller with a tax lien should clear it before listing so that title work does not hold up a closing.

sections.h2: When does a Ballard County bill become late?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets a single yearly rhythm for Kentucky counties unless the state approves a delay. Bills are payable until December 31 of the assessment year. Pay everything by November 1 and 2 percent comes off. Pay between then and year end and you owe the printed total. January adds a 5 percent penalty, and any later payment carries 10 percent.

The state revenue agency explains the next step. When business ends on April 15, unpaid bills pass to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency and a lien is recorded. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, and clerk and county attorney fees follow. If a delayed schedule is ever used, each stage becomes a one-month window, so check the dates printed on the bill with the sheriff's office.

sections.h2: What happens each year from January to December?
sections.html:
The Kentucky property tax year as it applies to a Ballard County parcel
Month or windowWhat occurs
January 1Value date for real estate
January 1 to March 1Real property listing window
First Monday in May, 13 daysPublic inspection of the tax roll
Day after inspection endsLast day to file an appeal with the clerk
25 to 35 days laterLocal board hears appeals for up to five days
December 31Bills due without penalty

Owners need not list real estate again if last year's roll described it completely and correctly and nothing major changed. Buyers may treat the deed price as the listed value for the following January 1.

sections.h2: How does a Ballard County appeal work?
sections.html:
Begin with a conference at the PVA, 132 North 4th Street. State rules bar a filing without one. Next, file with the County Clerk by the close of business on the workday after inspection ends, and write your own opinion of value on the form. The bill uses that opinion if it is printed before the case wraps up.

  • Bring proof: building and land descriptions, insurance policies, construction costs, sales listings.
  • A paid representative needs recognized credentials and your written authorization.
  • Audio recording of the hearing is your right.
  • If the board sets a higher value, a supplemental bill covers the difference.

An owner who never files with the local board, or files and then skips the hearing, cannot take the case to a later stage.

sections.h2: Do older residents in Ballard County get a discount?
sections.html:
Homeowners 65 or older, and those classified as totally disabled, can claim the state homestead exemption through the Ballard County PVA. It subtracts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026 and is adjusted every second year. The county has a lot of potential applicants: 21.4 percent of residents were 65 or older in 2020, the median age was 44.8, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate of 7,594 people is 1.8 percent below its April 2020 base.

An owner who never applied might be paying tax on value the state would exempt. A call to the PVA at (270) 335-3400 settles it.

sections.h2: What does a Ballard County house cost, and who lives in them?
sections.html:
In the 2020 to 2024 survey, the median owner-occupied home was valued at $145,800 and 76.0 percent of occupied homes were owned. Typical gross rent was $817 and income at the middle was $66,164. The county had 3,209 households and 3,730 housing units in 2025. The 2020 count put the vacancy rate at 12.4 percent of units and a rental vacancy rate of 12.0 percent.

Jobs are small in number: 155 employer establishments with 1,617 workers in 2023, up 19.2 percent in a year, and $87.0 million in payroll. The typical commute is 26.5 minutes. About 15.9 percent of residents are in poverty and 354 are veterans.

sections.h2: How do taxes work when a Ballard County house is sold?
sections.html:
The tax is a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date, and a recorded delinquency lien follows the property up to eleven years no matter who holds title. So the closing agent normally pays the year's bill out of the seller's proceeds. Ask the agent how the year will be divided between you and the buyer.

  • Ask the sheriff for current and past-due amounts.
  • Ask the clerk whether a lien is recorded.
  • Put a mailing address for the next bill in the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires.

An owner behind on taxes who inherited or left a river-county house can request a written cash offer. Any lien balance is deducted from the price at closing.

faqs.q: Who do I pay in Ballard County?
faqs.a: The Sheriff at 437 Ohio Street in Wickliffe. The county's elected-officials page lists (270) 335-3561 and (270) 335-5153.

faqs.q: How much do I save by paying early?
faqs.a: Two percent of the bill, if the sheriff receives payment in full by November 1. That is the rule in KRS 134.015, with the printed amount owed through December 31.
January brings a 5 percent penalty and later payments carry 10 percent. After April 15 the bill moves to the County Clerk and 1 percent monthly interest starts.

faqs.q: Where is an assessment appeal filed?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's office, 132 North 4th Street, once you have met with the PVA. The deadline is the workday following the end of inspection.

faqs.q: Is the homestead exemption a county program?
faqs.a: No, it is Kentucky's program, and the Ballard County PVA takes the application at (270) 335-3400. The 2025 and 2026 amount is $49,100 for owners 65 or older or totally disabled.
